title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: from election's inseparable help — certainty of causality, not bare science
pass_a_gloss: Fifthly, from the inseparable help of election or predestination we prove that it hangs not from our faith but from the mere good pleasure of God. For election imports a certainty of salvation as regards the elect man, and that not of bare science (for so to God from all eternity those things are most certain which are most fortuitous) but of causality, predestination so operating that it certainly leads the predestined to eternal life.
pass_b_english: Fifth argument: from election's inseparable help — it hangs not on our faith but on God's mere good pleasure. Election means certainty of salvation for the elect person: not bare knowledge (even the most chance events are utterly certain to God from eternity) but causality — predestination so working that it surely leads the predestined to eternal life.
source_text: Quinto, ab adjutorio inseparabili electionis sive praedestinationis probamus illam non ex fide nostra sed ex mero Dei beneplacito pendere. Nam electio importat certitudinem salutis quoad hominem electum, eamque non nudae scientiae (nam sic Deo ab omni aeternitate certissima sunt, quae sunt maxime fortuita) sed causalitatis, praedestinatione ita operante, ut certo perducat praedestinatum ad vitam aeternam.
